title: Integrality Gap of the Configuration LP for Restricted Santa Claus
short_statement: Determine the restricted Santa Claus configuration-LP gap, currently between $2$ and $53/15\approx3.5333$.
open_problem: Determine the exact integrality gap of the configuration LP for restricted max-min fair allocation.
background: Restricted Santa Claus, also called restricted max-min fair allocation, is the max-min analogue of scheduling and fair division. There are players and indivisible resources; each resource has a value and is acceptable only to some players. The goal is to allocate resources so that the least-valued player bundle is as large as possible. The configuration LP is the standard relaxation: for a guessed target value $T$, each player may fractionally choose configurations of resources whose total value is at least $T$. The LP is strong enough to certify constant-factor existence results, but rounding it constructively is difficult because feasible configurations form a hypergraph matching problem. The exact integrality gap of this LP is a central structural question: it measures the true power of the canonical relaxation independently of the current limitations of algorithms.
full_statement: In the restricted max-min fair allocation problem, let $P$ be a set of players and $R$ a set of indivisible resources. Each resource $r$ has a value $v_r\ge 0$, and each player $p$ either desires $r$ and values it at $v_r$, or does not desire it and values it at $0$. An allocation partitions resources among players and has value $\min_{p\in P}\sum_{r\in A_p} v_r$. For a target $T$, the configuration LP has one variable $x_{p,C}$ for every player $p$ and every subset $C\subseteq R_p$ with $\sum_{r\in C}v_r\ge T$; it requires each player to receive one unit of configurations and each resource to be used fractionally at most once. Let $T_{LP}$ be the largest feasible target and $T_{INT}$ the optimal integral allocation value. Determine the smallest universal constant $\gamma$ such that $T_{LP}\le \gamma T_{INT}$ for every restricted instance. Equivalently, close the gap between the best known lower-bound instances and the best known rounding/existence analyses for this canonical configuration LP.
known_results: Bansal and Sviridenko introduced the configuration-LP approach for Santa Claus-type allocation and showed why weaker assignment relaxations are inadequate. Asadpour, Feige, and Saberi proved that the restricted configuration LP has constant integrality gap at most $4$ using hypergraph matching and local-search ideas, but their existence proof did not by itself yield a polynomial-time $4$-approximation. Jansen and Rohwedder gave a shorter analysis improving the upper bound to $3+5/6$, and Cheng and Mao later improved it to $3+21/26\approx 3.808$ while also developing stronger constructive algorithms. On the lower-bound side, explicit instances show an integrality gap of at least $2$. The remaining gap interval is $[2,53/15]$. Haxell and Szabo (SODA 2023; Combinatorica 2025), Theorem 1.1, improve the restricted configuration-LP gap to $53/15$. This is existential, not a polynomial-time allocation algorithm.

progress.summary: The restricted configuration-LP gap lies in $[2,53/15]$; the upper bound is existential.

counterexample_rationale: Lower bounds are explicit finite allocation instances with a certified LP optimum and integral optimum. Such instances can be searched and checked computationally.
alphaevolve_rationale: Search over hypergraph allocation instances may find stronger LP gaps or patterns suggesting a tight family.

literature.synthesis: The restricted Santa Claus literature separates three questions: estimating the optimum via the configuration LP, proving existential integrality-gap bounds, and finding polynomial-time algorithms that construct allocations. The configuration LP is the natural relaxation for the first two questions, but its rounding is tied to difficult hypergraph matching local search. The historical $4$ and $3.808$ upper bounds, now improved to $53/15$, show substantial structure, while the lower bound $2$ leaves room for either sharper rounding or stronger gap constructions. A tight answer would clarify whether the algorithmic $4+\delta$ frontier is close to intrinsic LP limitations or mostly a constructive artifact.

agent_guidance.suitable_approaches: Search for high-gap hypergraph instances and compare against configuration-LP values. For upper bounds, inspect local-search expansion arguments and whether player/resource classifications can be sharpened.
agent_guidance.verification_notes: Distinguish integrality-gap results from polynomial-time approximation algorithms. A lower-bound claim must specify a finite family of restricted instances, prove a target $T$ is feasible in the configuration LP, and prove every integral allocation has value at most $T/\gamma$. An upper-bound claim must round every feasible $CLP(T)$ solution into an allocation of value at least $T/\gamma$ without assuming properties not implied by restricted valuations. Referees should check whether constants are normalized relative to $T_{LP}$ or the true optimum, and whether any local-search termination issue affects existence only or also algorithmic claims.
